knowledge:
- key_parameters: samplesheet=Path to a tab-delimited file describing the samples, targets, replicates, BAM files, and BED files ;; hets=A named character vector of filenames containing heterozygous SNPs for each group ;; CorrectWithgDNA=An optional named list of genomic DNA (gDNA) BAM files used to calculate background allelic ratios directly ;; min_mapq=Minimum MAPQ alignment quality score to include a read in pileup (default 15) ;; min_base_quality=Minimum base quality score to include a nucleotide in pileup (default 10) ;; RegionsToFilter=A named list of GRanges objects containing genomic regions to exclude (e.g., blacklists, high-coverage repeats) ;; RegionsToKeep=A named list of GRanges objects containing genomic regions to keep (e.g., unique mappability regions) ;; Iter=Number of iterations for the MCMC/Bayesian model in getASB (default 5000) ;; conf_level=Confidence level for the credible interval to call ASB (default 0.95) ;; RMcorrection=Logical indicating whether to apply reference mapping bias correction (default TRUE) ;; RAFcorrection=Logical indicating whether to apply relative allele frequency bias correction (default TRUE) ;; skipScriptRun=Logical indicating whether to skip the simulation and alignment steps in filterIntbias and use pre-computed simulated datasets (default FALSE)
- alternatives: None mentioned.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have ChIP-seq, FAIRE-seq, or similar functional genomic data and want to identify allele-specific binding or open chromatin events at heterozygous SNPs, particularly in cancer genomes where copy number alterations distort allele frequencies.
- pitfalls: Blacklist filters (e.g., blacklist_hg19) are designed for functional genomic data of short reads (20-100bp) and are not applicable to RNA-seq or other transcriptome data types. Unique mappability filters (e.g., UniqueMappability50bp_hg19) are specific to short reads (~50bp) and should not be applied to longer reads (>50bp). If both the RAF column in the hets files and the CorrectWithgDNA argument are missing, BaalChIP will not correct for copy-number bias.

workflows.name: asb_with_precomputed_raf
workflows.intent: Identify allele-specific binding events using pre-computed relative allele frequency (RAF) scores from heterozygous variant files.
input: MCF7_hetSNP.txt (tab-delimited heterozygous variant file with RAF column)
GM12891_hetSNP.txt (tab-delimited heterozygous variant file with RAF column)
bedFiles/ (directory containing ChIP-seq peak BED files)
workflows.stages: 1. Construct BaalChIP object ;; 2. Compute allele counts ;; 3. Filter problematic regions ;; 4. Filter intrinsic bias ;; 5. Merge replicates ;; 6. Filter out homozygous SNPs ;; 7. Run Bayesian ASB detection ;; 8. Generate final report
workflows.code:
res <- BaalChIP(samplesheet=samplesheet, hets=hets)
res <- alleleCounts(res, min_base_quality=10, min_mapq=15, verbose=FALSE)
res <- QCfilter(res, RegionsToFilter=list("blacklist"=blacklist_hg19, "highcoverage"=pickrell2011cov1_hg19), RegionsToKeep=list("UniqueMappability"=UniqueMappability50bp_hg19), verbose=FALSE)
res <- filterIntbias(res, simul_output=preComputed_output, tmpfile_prefix="c67c6ec6c433", skipScriptRun=TRUE, verbose=FALSE)
res <- mergePerGroup(res)
res <- filter1allele(res)
res <- getASB(res, Iter=5000, conf_level=0.95, cores = 4, RMcorrection = TRUE, RAFcorrection=TRUE)
result <- BaalChIP.report(res)

workflows.name: asb_with_gdna_bams
workflows.intent: Identify allele-specific binding events using genomic DNA (gDNA) BAM files to calculate relative allele frequency (RAF) scores.
input: bamFiles/ (directory containing ChIP-seq and gDNA BAM files)
bedFiles/ (directory containing ChIP-seq peak BED files)
workflows.stages: 1. Define gDNA BAM files list ;; 2. Construct BaalChIP object with CorrectWithgDNA ;; 3. Run the complete pipeline ;; 4. Generate final report
workflows.code:
gDNA <- list("TaT1"= c(file.path(wd, "bamFiles/TaT1_1_gDNA.test.bam"), file.path(wd, "bamFiles/TaT1_2_gDNA.test.bam")), "AMOVC"= c(file.path(wd, "bamFiles/AMOVC_1_gDNA.test.bam"), file.path(wd, "bamFiles/AMOVC_2_gDNA.test.bam")))
res2 <- BaalChIP(samplesheet=samplesheet, hets=hets, CorrectWithgDNA=gDNA)
res2 <- BaalChIP.run(res2, cores=4, verbose=TRUE)
result <- BaalChIP.report(res2)
